limits: Camera images are controlled2D affine raster scenes, not natural images or physical robot sensors.
Image pairs with different friction are deliberately identical; appearance cannot reveal friction in this contract.
The one-world-unit allowance is an authored family assumption tested here, not a statistical confidence interval.
Counts refer to captures/task instances. No probe, delivery attempt, learned model or physical robot trial occurs in this image-QA export.
Contact sheets enlarge192x192 pixels for review and add private annotations; the underlying PNGs are exact public payloads.

alias_replay.count_warning: The leaf count is an exact multiplicity sum, not billions of individually executed trials.

finite_transfer_calibration.factorization: 4 orientations × 2 shear signs × 4 subpixel phase pairs × 6 target centers
finite_transfer_calibration.scope: Finite 2D renderer support. Integer-translation invariance requires no clipping; palette/noise invariance follows from nonoverlapping bounded RGB supports. Not a physical sensor calibration guarantee.

image_http_client.transport: real authenticated loopback HTTP plus copied standalone public client

raster.oracle: Fraction geometry plus independently parsed pixels

robot_action_intersections.interpretation: Firm contact creates a common grip action only in the deliberately conditionable profile; resistant profiles require information or more contact than the strict deadline permits. Geometry sensing is still consequential for strict gate pairs.
robot_action_intersections.scope: Exhaustive seven terminal actions after listed prefixes, not an exact optimum over all sensing histories.

robot_transitions.oracle: exact decimal Fraction physical conditions plus independent time/energy/wear accounting
robot_transitions.scope: four selected prefixes, not every possible history; scripted controls only

small_policy_oracle.independence: full syntactic tree enumeration and raw world-path execution, no production belief recursion
small_policy_oracle.scope: 2 worlds, 2 one-use experiments with supports {0}, {1}, {0,1}, 2 actions; all 16 action success-set pairs

check.assurance: finite Python recurrence check; not a Lean proof or renderer refinement

report_description: An opaque roof hides which of two transport lanes is open. Moving to inspection exposes an actual PNG gate observation. Three visible fiducials establish the affine camera map. Camera changes, captures and probes consume simulated time, separately from synthetic tool cost.

A contact probe changes the surface through wear before returning a bounded friction interval. Gentle and firm contact therefore alter the later action conditions. Execution is terminal: a closed lane collides, insufficient traction slips, excessive fixture resistance stalls, and time or energy overruns prevent delivery.

rows: Fixed-pattern bounded noise; repeats are correlated.
Gentle adds 1 wear; firm adds 2. Reading refers to the changed surface.
A valid action commits once; delivery requires a successful route and mode within the public resource limits.

robotics_controls.comparison_description: Seven scripted controls each receive the same tools and cap over 216 episodes. The default twelve-seed protocol covers every joint deadline/contact profile: two thirds strict and one third relaxed, with equal contact-profile counts. Tool budget: 30. Simulated deadlines: 10 strict, 26 relaxed.
findings: The minimal fixed sequence is a strong comparator: inspection plus a gentle probe suffices. The budget-aware reference skips sensing when the public deadline permits a slow detour. Its sensing schedule depends on that known contract; this is not a demonstrated observation-contingent sensing advantage.

Firm contact moves both initial regimes into the grip-safe range in the conditionable profile. The resistant profile preserves a case where this common-mode guarantee fails. The fixed-grip variant still succeeds on favorable individual states; complete-pair success exposes its missing guarantee.

Pixel blanking and paired swaps test the route-selection sensor path. A deliberately false low-friction interval disrupts measurement-based handling, while firm-then-fixed-grip ignores that reading by construction. All physical wear and tool costs remain charged during these interventions.
Relaxed reference episodes skip both sensors and are unexposed controls in the sensor interventions. Strict-profile results isolate episodes that actually receive the altered observation.

manual_visual_review.scope: Visual presentation review supplements executable checks; it does not establish pixel-level correctness, statistical generalization or real-camera coverage.

manual_robotics_review.method: Multimodal visual inspection of all 18 full-size contact-sheet PNGs, one sheet per view_image call. Source observation images appear as nearest-neighbor 240-pixel panels; no scratch resizing was used.
manual_robotics_review.scope: All 288 overview and inspection capture panels across train, dev, transfer; difficulties 1, 2, 3; seeds 0 through 7; both twins.
findings: Every overview visibly covers the full possible opening region; no opening is visible through the roof.
Inspection exposes exactly one green opening on the gate, with all three colored calibration fiducials in frame.
Gate twins visibly change the opening location in inspection while overview appearance remains the same.
Friction twins have visually identical observations at each view while private evaluator friction annotations differ; exact full-payload identity is independently checked by the exporter.
Transfer panels visibly include rotated, reflected, and sheared geometry; upper/lower labels denote calibrated world routes and need not coincide with screen vertical position.
Increasing RGB noise is visible in difficulty-3 panels without obscuring the advertised high-contrast palette.
All reviewed headings, view labels, private annotations, and resource captions fit their cards without observed overlap or clipping.
Time/energy/wear captions are consistent across overview (1/0/0) and inspection (3/1/0) panels.
No visual defects requiring a source change were found.
limitations: This is AI-assisted development QA, not a human perceptual study or a scored learned-model trial.
Visual inspection does not establish exact byte identity or numeric accuracy; those are separate automated manifest checks.
These are controlled 2D raster observations of a finite simulator, not natural images or physical robot experiments.
Capture-only QA performs no robot delivery; task-completion evidence is reported in the separate controller study.
